body.statement: Along every subsequence extracted by \(\mathrm{lem:local-subsequence-extraction}\), \(H_\ell\to H\), and there is one coupling carrying deterministic local objects \(d\), \(h\), and \(H\), together with all components of one jointly Gaussian vector \((g,Z)\) whose pre and post blocks are independent. On this coupling, jointly over post periods, \(v_\ell\to V_h\), \(A_{t,\ell}(v_\ell)\to A_t(V_h)\), \(\Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}\to\Psi_t(d,Z)\), and \(B_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow B_t(d,Z)\). The pre-weight--post-quantile cross contribution obeys \(\sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell}[-2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}v_\ell^\top B_{t,\ell}]\Rightarrow-2V_h^\top B_t(d,Z)\), but it vanishes at every headline loss scale: multiplication by \(\sqrt{m_\ell}\) gives coefficient \(n_\ell^{-1/2}\) when \(\rho_\ell\to\infty\) or \(\rho_\ell\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), multiplication by \(n_\ell\) gives coefficient \(\sqrt{n_\ell/m_\ell}\) when \(\rho_\ell\to0\), and division by \(a_\ell\) gives coefficient \(\sqrt{n_\ell}/(n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell})\to0\). The three remaining \(\epsilon_{t,\ell}\) terms vanish on the same scales. Consequently, whenever \(\omega=\lim n_\ell/(n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell})\), \(E_{t,\ell}/a_\ell\Rightarrow(1-\omega)A_t(V_h)+\omega\Psi_t(d,Z)\). Equivalently, if \(\rho_\ell\to\infty\), then \(\sqrt{m_\ell}E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z)\); if \(\rho_\ell\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), then \(\sqrt{m_\ell}E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z)+A_t(V_h)/\kappa\); and if \(\rho_\ell\to0\), then \(n_\ell E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow A_t(V_h)\). The endpoint component is zero almost surely if and only if each almost-sure affine-endpoint equality class has coefficient sum zero, while the quadratic component is zero almost surely if and only if all donor post quantile functions coincide almost everywhere.
body.proof_tex:
The pre empirical processes in \(\mathrm{thm:face\mbox{-}weight\mbox{-}limit}\) and the post empirical processes are independent by \(\mathrm{ass:cell\mbox{-}independence}\).  The cited empirical-CDF functional central limit theorem therefore supplies a joint Gaussian limit \((g,Z)\) with independent pre and post blocks and the within-cell bridge covariance
\[
 \operatorname{Cov}(Z_{jtr},Z_{jtr'})=\min(c_{jtr},c_{jtr'})-c_{jtr}c_{jtr'},
 \qquad \operatorname{Cov}(Z_{jtr},Z_{j'tr'})=0\quad(j\neq j').
\]
The cited Skorokhod representation theorem permits this joint weak convergence to be realized on one probability space with almost-sure convergence; this is the coupling asserted in the statement.

Within a finite root-\(m_\ell\) knot cluster, subtracting a common translation and using
\(\sqrt{m_\ell}(\widehat c-c)=Z_\ell\) changes the separately anchored pairs to
\[
 (a,d+Z_\ell),\qquad(-a,d).
\]
Between macro clusters, pulse supports are eventually disjoint.  Thus the exact squared norm is the sum of the cluster energies.  Convergence of jump coefficients, offsets, and Gaussian coordinates, together with the separation-free Lipschitz inequality in
\(\mathrm{lem:endpoint\mbox{-}identity}\), gives jointly in \(t\)
\[
 \Psi^{\mathrm{fin}}_{t,\ell}\longrightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z).
\]
The argmin proof gives \(v_\ell\to V_h\) on the same coupling.  Since
\(M_{t,\ell}\to M_t\), continuity of a quadratic form gives
\[
 A_{t,\ell}(v_\ell)\longrightarrow V_h^\top M_tV_h=A_t(V_h).
\]
Finally, the finite post laws make \(B_{t,\ell}\) a finite sum of integrals over the same shrinking pulse intervals.  After multiplying their lengths by \(\sqrt{m_\ell}\), endpoint convergence on every local ordering cell gives the finite limit denoted by \(B_t(d,Z)\); ties have probability zero unless the corresponding affine Gaussian endpoints agree almost surely, in which case the separately anchored formula gives the same value from either adjacent cell.  Hence \(B_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow B_t(d,Z)\), jointly with the preceding limits.

The exact expansion now gives
\[
 \sqrt{n_\ell m_\ell}\left[-2(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}
 v_\ell^\top B_{t,\ell}\right]
 \Rightarrow-2V_h^\top B_t(d,Z).
\]
At the endpoint scale \(\sqrt{m_\ell}\), its coefficient is \(n_\ell^{-1/2}\); at the weight scale \(n_\ell\), it is
\(\sqrt{n_\ell/m_\ell}=\rho_\ell/\sqrt{n_\ell}\); and after division by \(a_\ell\), it is
\[
 \frac{(n_\ell m_\ell)^{-1/2}}{n_\ell^{-1}+m_\ell^{-1/2}}
 =\frac{\sqrt{n_\ell}}{n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
The bounds in \(\mathrm{thm:finite\mbox{-}two\mbox{-}source\mbox{-}expansion}\) show that all three \(\epsilon\)-terms vanish at these same applicable scales.  Moreover
\[
 \frac{n_\ell^{-1}}{a_\ell}=\frac{\sqrt{m_\ell}}{n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell}}=1-\omega_\ell,\qquad
 \frac{m_\ell^{-1/2}}{a_\ell}=\frac{n_\ell}{n_\ell+\sqrt{m_\ell}}=\omega_\ell.
\]
Slutsky's theorem therefore yields
\[
 \frac{E_{t,\ell}}{a_\ell}\Rightarrow
 (1-\omega)A_t(V_h)+\omega\Psi_t(d,Z).
\]
Taking respectively \(\rho_\ell\to\infty\), \(\rho_\ell\to\kappa\in(0,\infty)\), and \(\rho_\ell\to0\) gives
\[
 \sqrt{m_\ell}E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z),\qquad
 \sqrt{m_\ell}E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow\Psi_t(d,Z)+\kappa^{-1}A_t(V_h),
\]
and
\[
 n_\ell E_{t,\ell}\Rightarrow A_t(V_h),
\]
because in the last case the endpoint coefficient is \(\rho_\ell\to0\).

For endpoint degeneracy, apply the exact zero criterion to the finite affine Gaussian endpoint list.  Two endpoints from different almost-sure equality classes coincide with probability zero, since their difference is a nonzero affine Gaussian variable.  Finiteness then shows that the realized equality partition equals the almost-sure partition with probability one.  Hence \(\Psi_t=0\) almost surely exactly when the coefficients sum to zero within every almost-sure equality class.  The quadratic criterion is the one proved in \(\mathrm{thm:face\mbox{-}weight\mbox{-}limit}\).
